author_note: This report's pairwise evidence quotes A9's metric values (P3 0.418, P8a 0.8108) as the candidate's and A10's as the baseline's; its criteria verdicts also cite A9 numbers. Recorded as returned; treat its pairwise call as low-confidence noise.
reads_as_reason: Block head, slab torso and very wide A-pose arms read as a Roblox-style figure, not a calm adult product. The change from the baseline is cosmetic.

G1.evidence: The head is a rounded cube with a visor window. The chest is a wide box with a flat top ledge. The arms are straight tapered slabs that flare out to about 0.42 H wide (metrics P3 = 0.418, band 0.22-0.29). The pelvis is a separate box hanging off the waist band. The side view shows a large square back pack and a block-shaped heel. None of this reads as the human-proportioned Optimus or Atlas family.

G2.evidence: Chest, waist and pelvis are three separate masses, with a dark band between chest and pelvis and a horizontal ledge where the pelvis box starts (front clay view). The front silhouette has a hard shoulder shelf and then arm wedges that meet the torso at an abrupt notch. Thigh and shank are straight columns. Thigh and shank taper are 0.8108 and 0.8639 against bands of 0.65 and 0.60, and the calf's widest point is 0.3933 of the way down against a band of 0.33. Joint recesses (elbow, knee) are present as dark bands, but they sit between blocky shells rather than flowing forms.

G3.evidence: Two-tone view: warm-white shells, graphite recesses and a black visor, with no accent colour. The knee and elbow dark bands are cleaner than in the baseline. The boundary between white and graphite is still jagged on the left-view elbow and forearm and at the shank sides.

G4.evidence: Section squareness and radii differ between segments. The head, chest and pelvis are near-square boxes with small radii. The thigh and shank are softer oval columns. The arms are flat-sided slabs. The back pack is a hard-edged block. This does not look like one radius family. The new chest oval and the small slot on the forearm in the candidate are one-off details that match nothing else on the body.

G6.evidence: At equal height the design is much wider than optimus_like and atlas_like (front IoU 0.5332 and 0.5657). Matching features: head height is in band (P1 = 0.14), and hip and knee heights are in band (0.50 and 0.27). Features that do not match: the shoulder and arm span is far outside the references' narrow shoulder line, the neck is nearly absent (P2a = 0.1143, band 0.18-0.55), the legs are columns where the references have long tapered legs, and the foot is long and bricklike (P10a = 0.238, band 0.13-0.17).

pairwise.evidence: Low confidence; the two are close to identical. I looked at the baseline first and judged by gestalt. The candidate's two-tone view has a cleaner knee and shank, with the ragged dark patch on the shank side in the baseline replaced by a clean band. Its leg and back panel breaks are slightly more finished-looking, and its taper numbers are marginally better (thigh 0.8108 vs 0.8648, shank 0.8639 vs 0.913, calf widest 0.3933 vs 0.4533). Against that, its shoulders are slightly wider (0.418 vs 0.412), the ledge count and total went up (5 vs 4, 1.2877 vs 0.8841), and it adds chest and forearm marks that do not belong in a D1 step. Neither changes the toy reading. The net improvement is small.

top_changes.change: Narrow the shoulder and arm span, which is the main departure from both references. Bring the outer width from about 0.42 H toward about 0.28 H, and let the arms hang closer to the body. Reduce the chest top width and the arm_core and upper arm widths together, so the shoulder-to-waist line becomes a taper and not a shelf.
top_changes.profile_param: segments[chest].stations[shoulder].w (and segments[arm_core].stations[*].w; arm cy toward the body)

top_changes.change: Make the leg a flowing form with a real taper. Put the thigh's widest section at the hip and cut the knee section to about 0.8 of the hip width. Move the calf bulge up to the top third of the shank and cut the ankle section strongly. Remove the pelvis box overhang by blending the pelvis into the waist band with a larger-radius, more rounded section.
top_changes.profile_param: segments[thigh].stations[knee].w and .d; segments[shank].stations[calf].z and stations[ankle].w; segments[pelvis].stations[top].n

top_changes.change: Remove the box reading from the head and chest. Raise n (roundness) on the head and on the chest at the shoulder and waist stations. Lengthen the neck so it is visible. Shorten the foot and lower the heel block so the foot looks like a shoe and not a brick.

notes: I judged from the clay views, the two-tone views and the silhouette lineup. The A9 and A10 sheets are almost pixel-identical, so the pairwise call rests on small differences in the two-tone view and the metrics. All numbers are quoted from the metrics JSON. The images do not contradict any metric. The reference outlines are silhouettes only, so G6 covers proportion and outline, not surface language. The new chest oval and forearm slot in the candidate are surface detail, which D1 says comes later.
